reason: Terminated by statutory repeal on 1935-06-14. EO 6885-A (October 25, 1934, Franklin D. Roosevelt) incorporates by reference the annexed report of the National Industrial Recovery Board, finds that the amended code complies with Title I, orders 'that the Code as amended be and it is hereby approved' and modifies 'the previous approval of said Code ... to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as amended' (the Builders Supplies Trade code). The order states no period, condition or date of its own, so it has no own-terms end. Its operative effect depended on section 3 of Title I: under 3(b) the approved code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, a violation in or affecting interstate commerce was an unfair method of competition, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and under 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor. Section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 (49 Stat. 375, chapter 246, approved June 14, 1935) provides 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed' and states no later effective date, so the approval's prospective operative effect ended when the resolution was approved.
